A1.justification: Both complete 37-page PDFs describe LINGOLY-TOO and include matching main sections and Appendices A–M. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v6 reports original LLM benchmark evaluations in Section 4, tokenisation experiments in Appendix K, and results from a 172-participant human study in Appendix L.

after.justification: v7 retains the same original LLM evaluations, tokenisation experiments, and human-study results in Section 4 and Appendices K–L.

M1.justification: The expert-designed grapheme permutations, annotation and generation procedures, and evaluation pipeline are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices B–C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 82 UKLO problems, five additional UKLO 2025 problems, and six-problem human-study subset, with unchanged language, task, and participant coverage.

E2.justification: The main-evaluation model variants and experiment-specific comparators are unchanged, including those in Figures 1 and 6, Tables 2 and 9, and the guided-reasoning and tokenisation experiments.

E3.justification: Exact-match evaluation, permutation counts, prompting, model configurations, tokenisation procedures, and human-study assignment and inclusion criteria remain identical.

E4.justification: Both retain the same no-context, permutation-sensitivity, language-resourcedness, tokenisation, reasoning-trace, expert-guidance, and human-study robustness analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

E5.justification: The 500-sample bootstrap procedure, standard errors, confidence intervals, Bonferroni correction, and human-study statistical tests and regression procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative outcomes match, including the main model scores in Figures 1 and 6, UKLO 2025 results in Table 9, and human-study results in Tables 13–15.

T1.justification: The score definitions in Sections 3.4 and 4.2–4.3 and the structure-preserving permutation definitions and mathematical examples in Appendix B are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about benchmark difficulty, quantifying knowledge effects, and generating uncontaminated reasoning problems.

C2.justification: Interpretations of knowledge shortcuts and obfuscation sensitivity, the limitations in Section 5, and the human-study explanations and qualifications in Appendix L.4 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Annotation instructions, prompt templates, model identifiers, hardware details, processing procedures, and code/data access and licensing information are unchanged. The funding-credit additions do not revise technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, comparison with existing Olympiad obfuscation practices, and bibliography are identical; no cited work or research positioning changes.

P1.justification: v7 adds K.K. to the Clarendon scholarship and Dieter Schwarz-funded research-programme acknowledgments on page 11, removes a trailing author-list comma, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–15 retain identical content, formatting, captions, and placement. The acknowledgment edit remains within the existing paragraph layout.

improvement.justification: v7 makes funding attribution more complete and fixes an author-list punctuation error. All scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations, reproducibility information, and visual displays remain unchanged, so these administrative corrections do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
